The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debate/?id=2025-03-25.115.1) to agree with the main idea of the bill. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill for a second time, which means it can now be considered in more detail. ### What does this bill do? This bill limits the circumstances in which the Minister has to the power to reconsider past decisions in order to create greater stability for certain projects. According for the [explanatory memorandum](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22legislation%2Fems%2Fr7323_ems_129d226c-7198-4ca1-9f62-b01fdae1fa59%22;rec=0), which is a political document prepared by the Government, who introduced the bill: > *The 2021 State of the Environment Report made clear that all aspects of the Australian environment are under stress, and many are declining. Multiple pressures from factors like climate change, habitat loss, invasive species, and pollution create cumulative impacts that amplify threats to our environment. Better information, along with the increasingly dynamic nature of the environment increases the likelihood that actions originally determined to be unlikely to have a significant impact on a protected matter under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999 (EPBC Act) could in future meet the threshold for reconsideration.* > > *Under the EPBC Act, an action can be lawfully taken if the Minister decides that it is not a controlled action. In contrast, if the Minister decides that the action is a controlled action, the action is subject to further assessment under the EPBC Act and cannot be taken unless and until the Minister approves the taking of the action. The EPBC Act requires the Minister to decide that an action is a controlled action if the Minister is satisfied that the action has, will have, or is likely to have, a significant impact on a protected matter.* > >

Moved procedural arrangements to sequence debate and votes on Supply Bills, the Transport Security Amendment Bill 2024, the Parliamentary Business Resources Legislation Amendment Bill 2025 and the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment Bill 2025. Argued that Australians distrust the major parties because they lack transparency and prioritise political careers, then criticised Labor's energy policy and its Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Reconsiderations) Bill 2025. Claimed the bill would give salmon companies an environmental exemption for electoral advantage and harm Tasmania's brand.

Moved and amended a Senate business motion setting meeting hours, ordering consideration and expedited voting on listed bills, providing for valedictory statements and budget responses, allowing divisions after 6.30 pm, and adding further bills before the motion was agreed to.

Argued that the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Reconsiderations) Bill 2025 would end reconsideration proceedings affecting salmon farming and the maugean skate, while also criticising delays to the North West Shelf project and warning of consequences for Western Australian jobs, energy and investment.

The Minister would set the categories and number of targets, which could be numeric or action-based, through a new instrument to the Act.

The same number of senators voted for and against paragraph (a), placitum (ii) of the [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2025-02-13.21.1) as moved by Queensland Senator [Larissa Waters](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/queensland/larissa_waters) (Greens), which means it failed to pass. ### Motion text > *That—* > > *(a) the questions on all remaining stages of the following bills be put at 1 pm: [...]* > >> *(ii) Workplace Gender Equality Amendment (Setting Gender Equality Targets) Bill 2024;*

Moved to require questions on all stages of the Early Childhood Education and Care (Three Day Guarantee) Bill 2025 to be put after a message from the House of Representatives, while allowing committee consideration to continue; leave to add another bill was not granted.

Debate supported amendments to the Workplace Gender Equality Amendment (Setting Gender Equality Targets) Bill 2024, which would require designated employers with 500 or more employees to select and report on three gender equality targets over three years. Concerns were raised about compliance burdens for over 1,650 businesses, while supporters argued the obligations should extend to employers with 100 or more workers and include targets to reduce the gender pay gap.

Supported the Workplace Gender Equality Amendment (Setting Gender Equality Targets) Bill 2024 but moved amendments to extend obligations to employers with fewer workers, require targets that close gender pay gaps, and prevent government contracts going to employers that fail to address them. Also criticised the coalition's record on women's equality and urged passage of the bill.

Argued that the Workplace Gender Equality Amendment (Setting Gender Equality Targets) Bill 2024 would require large employers to set measurable, transparent gender equality targets. The bill was presented as building on workplace data and transparency measures, including action on gender pay gaps and gender diversity in leadership. Debate was interrupted.

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2025-02-06.45.1) to agree with the main idea of the bill. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill for a second time. This means they can now consider the bill in greater detail. ### What is the bill's main idea? According to the [bill homepage](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r7277), the bill: > *Amends the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 to separate the Australian Energy Regulator (AER) from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and establish the AER as a non-corporate Commonwealth entity.*

The MP argued that the Safeguard Mechanism (Crediting) Amendment Bill 2022, backed by Labor and the Greens, will block 116 coal, oil and gas projects—including Woodside’s Scarborough and Shell’s Crux fields—risking jobs for 60,000 FIFO workers in Western Australia and causing deindustrialisation, while household electricity prices are set to rise 56% over two years.

The speaker supported the $15.9 billion Appropriation Bills (No. 3 and No. 4) 2021-2022, detailing $2.86 billion for the Department of Health’s COVID-19 response, $2.75 billion for the NDIS, $1.41 billion for education and employment, and $1.28 billion for defence, while also advocating for federal funding for numerous local infrastructure projects in the City of Joondalup and City of Stirling, including the $15.7 million Heathridge Park redevelopment, coastal paths, and park upgrades.

The speaker supported the Religious Discrimination Bill 2021, arguing it adds protections for people based on religion, matching existing protections for age, sex, race or disability. The speaker cited 61% of Australians (14 million) as religious, noted instances of religious discrimination including personal media attacks for being Christian, and argued religious institutions should be able to preference staff who adhere to their faith.

The speaker supported the appropriation bills, arguing the budget prioritises vaccination and economic recovery while delivering record federal funding to Western Australia, including $13.2 billion in total payments, $5.3 billion in GST, $1.6 billion for infrastructure, and $2.8 billion for health.
Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency (Charges) Bill 2021

The speaker supported the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency (Charges) Bill 2021 and related amendment, which phase in increased cost recovery for TEQSA from 15% to full cost by 2024, and noted $245 million in federal funding for Edith Cowan University's new Perth campus, set to open in 2025 with $695 million total cost.
Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency Amendment (Cost Recovery) Bill 2021
